issues.body: The design explicitly defines a workflow as non-inert when any selector-gated step reads it, but `test_o3_no_rust_ci_workflow_references_an_inert_workflow` only searches the YAML text for each inert file's literal basename. It misses a denylisted workflow invoking a script that reads that workflow, and it misses directory/glob-based reads such as `.github/workflows/*.yml`. Therefore the test does not establish the stated O3 obligation, and the inert-by-default policy can silently skip relevant CI when such an input exists or is introduced later.
issues.fix_hint: Make dependency discovery cover step inputs transitively, including invoked repository scripts and directory/glob reads, or narrow the policy so inertness is allowlisted where dependencies can be audited. Add a negative fixture in which a denylisted workflow invokes a helper that reads an otherwise-inert workflow (and another using a workflow-directory glob), and require the gate to fail or classify that workflow as Rust-CI-relevant.
issues.title: O3 does not cover indirect or non-literal workflow inputs

verdict.summary: The inversion is not yet backed by the proof claimed in the change. O3 checks only literal workflow filenames appearing directly in denylisted workflow YAML, but selector-gated jobs can read workflow files indirectly through invoked scripts or via directory/glob inputs. Such a dependency would remain invisible and an affected workflow would be classified inert, allowing the Rust matrix to be skipped after one of its inputs changes.
